project.name: green-life
project.description: Green Life is a React Native mobile app for scanning or searching products and returning source-backed environmental impact data. It is built with Expo and TypeScript and includes navigation, theme tokens, and starter screens aligned to a Figma spec.

nodes.name: App.tsx
nodes.summary: Root React Native component that bootstraps the app with font loading, React Query, dark-themed navigation container, and splash screen management.

nodes.name: babel.config.js
nodes.summary: Babel configuration that enables the Expo preset for React Native transpilation.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Application entry point that registers the root App component with Expo's registerRootComponent.

nodes.name: mock-api-server.js
nodes.summary: Standalone HTTP mock server that simulates the Green Life REST API (v1) with hardcoded product, source, history, saved-items, and search endpoints for UI development.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain Node.js http module with no framework dependencies; uses URL constructor for route parsing.

nodes.name: lookup.ts
nodes.summary: Express controller factory for POST /api/v1/lookup/image that routes image lookups through food (Vision -> DB -> USDA -> Climatiq) and material (Vision -> DB) pipelines, awarding Sparks on success.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses factory pattern returning a closure that captures injected service instances.

nodes.name: search.ts
nodes.summary: Express controller factory for GET /api/v1/search that extends product search with a 'food' mode, looking up carbon impact data from the food emission table with optional USDA enrichment and Sparks rewards.

nodes.name: food_emission_factors.ts
nodes.summary: Database seed file containing a comprehensive array of farm-to-fork CO2e emission factors per kg for ~50 food categories (beef, poultry, seafood, vegetables, etc.) sourced from Agribalyse, IPCC, and Poore & Nemecek, plus a seeder function.
nodes.languageNotes: Primarily a large typed constant array with an async seed function at the end.

nodes.name: material_impacts.ts
nodes.summary: Database seed file with lifecycle impact data for disposable restaurant materials (straws, cups, lids, utensils, containers) including CO2e per unit, recyclability, decomposition time, and better alternatives.

nodes.name: climatiqService.ts
nodes.summary: Last-resort carbon estimation service that calls the Climatiq API with EXIOBASE IO tables when a food item cannot be matched in the local emission factor table or USDA, returning category-level low-confidence estimates.

nodes.name: createLookupController
nodes.summary: Factory function that instantiates all restaurant lookup services (food, material, sparks, vision, USDA, Climatiq) and returns an Express handler supporting product, food, and material image lookup modes.

nodes.name: createSearchController
nodes.summary: Factory function that creates an Express search handler supporting product pass-through and food carbon impact search with USDA enrichment and Sparks rewards.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Helper that writes a JSON response with CORS headers in the standard {data, meta, error} envelope format.

nodes.name: ClimatiqService
nodes.summary: Service class that estimates food carbon footprint via Climatiq's EXIOBASE emission factors, mapping food names to broad categories and converting per-dollar estimates to per-serving values.

nodes.name: seedFoodEmissionFactors
nodes.summary: Async function that inserts the FOOD_EMISSION_FACTORS array into the PostgreSQL food_emission_factors table using upsert (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).

nodes.name: seedMaterialImpacts
nodes.summary: Async function that inserts the MATERIAL_IMPACTS array into the PostgreSQL material_impacts table using upsert (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).

nodes.name: foodEmissionService.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a multi-strategy food carbon emission lookup service that queries a PostgreSQL food_emission_factors table using exact match, alias containment, pg_trgm fuzzy matching, and category-level fallback to return kg CO2e impact data per food item.

nodes.name: FoodEmissionService
nodes.summary: Database-backed service that resolves food names to carbon emission impact data using a four-stage lookup chain (exact, alias, fuzzy trigram, category fallback) against a PostgreSQL food_emission_factors table.

nodes.name: materialImpactService.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a multi-strategy restaurant material sustainability lookup service that queries a PostgreSQL material_impacts table to return recyclability, compostability, disposal guidance, and CO2e data for items like straws, cups, and containers.

nodes.name: MaterialImpactService
nodes.summary: Database-backed service that resolves material descriptions (e.g. 'plastic straw') to sustainability impact data using exact, alias, fuzzy, and item-type fallback matching against a material_impacts table.

nodes.name: sparksService.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the Sparks gamification system that awards points to users for photo scans, menu lookups, and table scans, including a first-scan bonus, with transactional PostgreSQL persistence and summary/history retrieval.

nodes.name: SparksService
nodes.summary: Transactional service that awards and tracks 'Sparks' gamification points per user, with first-scan bonus logic, running totals, and paginated history retrieval from PostgreSQL.

nodes.name: usdaService.ts
nodes.summary: Optional enrichment service that fetches nutritional data (calories, protein) from the USDA FoodData Central API to augment food emission results with real nutrition context.

nodes.name: UsdaService
nodes.summary: Calls the USDA FoodData Central search API to enrich a food name with calorie and protein data, returning null gracefully if the API is unavailable.

nodes.name: visionService.ts
nodes.summary: Wraps the Google Cloud Vision API to identify food items and disposable restaurant materials in photos, filtering raw labels through curated keyword lists to produce domain-relevant results.

nodes.name: VisionService
nodes.summary: Calls Google Cloud Vision API with LABEL_DETECTION and WEB/OBJECT_LOCALIZATION features, then filters results through food and material keyword lists to classify photographed restaurant items.

nodes.name: restaurant.ts
nodes.summary: Defines shared TypeScript request/response types for the restaurant API layer (image lookup, search, food/material response envelopes) and exports a buildCarbonEquivalents utility that converts kg CO2e into human-relatable comparisons.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports types from sibling service files, creating a cross-reference between server types and service layer. The buildCarbonEquivalents function is the only runtime export.

nodes.name: buildCarbonEquivalents
nodes.summary: Converts a kg CO2e value into an array of human-relatable equivalents (miles driven, phone charges, tree absorption days, streaming hours) using EPA conversion factors.

nodes.name: claude.ts
nodes.summary: Client-side wrapper that sends user messages to the Anthropic Claude API (Haiku model) with sustainability-focused system instructions and item context for the voice chat feature.

nodes.name: askClaude
nodes.summary: Sends a user message with scanned item context to the Claude Haiku API and returns the text response, used for the voice-based sustainability assistant feature.

nodes.name: client.ts
nodes.summary: Central API fetch wrapper that routes requests through either a mock data layer or the real Green Life API based on an environment variable, providing typed JSON response handling and error propagation.

nodes.name: apiFetch
nodes.summary: Generic typed fetch wrapper that delegates to mockFetch when USE_MOCK_API is enabled, otherwise calls the real API base URL with JSON content headers and error handling.

nodes.name: items.ts
nodes.summary: Thin API module that exposes a single getItemDetail function for fetching full item details by ID through the shared apiFetch client.

nodes.name: getItemDetail
nodes.summary: Fetches a single item's full detail by ID from the /items/:id endpoint, returning a typed ApiEnvelope containing the ItemDetail.

nodes.name: lookup.ts
nodes.summary: Provides API functions for product lookup by barcode, text search, and image recognition, all delegating to the shared apiFetch client.

nodes.name: lookupBarcode

nodes.name: search

nodes.name: mockFetch

layers.name: Screens & Navigation
layers.description: App entry points, React Navigation stack/tab configuration, and all screen-level components that compose the user-facing views for scanning, searching, and viewing environmental impact data.

layers.name: UI Components
layers.description: Reusable React Native presentational components including generic UI primitives (buttons, cards, states), item display badges, metric rows, and restaurant-specific impact cards.

layers.name: Data Access & Hooks
layers.description: Client-side API modules for product lookup, user data, and external AI services, plus React hooks that orchestrate data fetching, mutations, and local state synchronization via React Query and Zustand.

layers.name: Server
layers.description: Express backend with controllers for image lookup and search, domain services for food emissions, material impacts, vision recognition, USDA nutrition, Climatiq carbon estimation, Sparks gamification, database seed data, and shared server types.

layers.name: Foundation
layers.description: Design system tokens (colors, typography, spacing, radius, shadows), shared TypeScript type definitions for the domain and API contracts, and build configuration.

layers.name: Tooling
layers.description: Development utilities including the standalone mock API server for offline UI development and Python scripts for generating branded product documentation from Markdown sources.

tour.title: App Bootstrap
tour.description: Start at the application entry point. index.js registers the root component via Expo's registerRootComponent, which hands off to App.tsx. App.tsx bootstraps the entire application by loading custom fonts (PlusJakartaSans), initializing React Query for server state management, wrapping everything in a dark-themed NavigationContainer, and managing the splash screen lifecycle. This is the single point where all top-level providers and configurations converge.
tour.languageLesson: React Native apps use registerRootComponent instead of ReactDOM.render. Expo abstracts platform-specific bootstrapping (AppRegistry on iOS/Android) behind this single call.

tour.title: Domain Types
tour.description: Before exploring any features, understand the vocabulary of the codebase. domain.ts defines the core data shapes -- ProductSummary, ImpactMetric, ItemDetail, HistoryItem, and UserProfile -- along with union types like MatchType (exact, probable, estimate) and EstimateType that communicate data confidence to users. api.ts provides the generic ApiEnvelope<T> wrapper that standardizes all API responses with data, meta, and error fields. Every screen, API call, and component speaks this shared language.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript union types like 'exact' | 'probable' | 'estimate' create exhaustive, compiler-checked enumerations without the overhead of enums. The generic ApiEnvelope<T> pattern enforces a consistent response shape across all endpoints.

tour.title: Design System Tokens
tour.description: The theme system is the most widely imported module in the codebase, used by virtually every UI component and screen. The barrel file src/theme/index.ts re-exports five token modules: colors (dark forest palette targeting WCAG AA), typography (PlusJakartaSans font scale), spacing (4px-to-40px scale), radius (sm through pill), and shadows (card elevation). This design-token architecture ensures visual consistency and makes global theme changes trivial -- change one token, update the entire app.
tour.languageLesson: Barrel files (index.ts that re-exports) create a clean public API surface. Consumers import from 'src/theme' rather than reaching into individual token files, which allows internal restructuring without breaking imports.

tour.title: Navigation Architecture
tour.description: Navigation defines how users move through the app. RootNavigator.tsx sets up a native stack with the complete screen hierarchy: onboarding, authentication, main tabs, barcode scanning, photo capture, and detail screens. MainTabs.tsx configures the bottom tab navigator with five tabs (Home, Search, Saved, Profile, Ask) using Feather icons. types.ts defines RootStackParamList and MainTabParamList for type-safe navigation -- every navigation.navigate() call is checked at compile time against these param lists.
tour.languageLesson: React Navigation's TypeScript integration uses ParamList type maps (e.g., RootStackParamList) to enforce that every navigate() call passes the correct parameters for each route. This prevents runtime crashes from missing or mistyped route params.

tour.title: Shared UI Components
tour.description: The components/ui directory provides the reusable building blocks that every screen assembles from. Screen.tsx wraps content in SafeAreaView with consistent background and padding. PrimaryButton and SecondaryButton offer size/variant combinations for CTAs. LoadingState, ErrorState, and EmptyState handle the three async data states that appear on nearly every screen. SearchBar, StatCard, and BrandFooter round out the shared kit. These components consume theme tokens directly, so the design system from Step 3 flows through every pixel.

tour.title: API Client Layer
tour.description: The API client module mediates all server communication. client.ts provides the central apiFetch wrapper, which checks an environment variable to route requests through either mockData.ts (for offline development) or the real Green Life server. This mock/real toggle is the key architectural decision -- it lets the frontend team iterate on screens without a running backend. The domain-specific modules (items.ts, lookup.ts, sources.ts, user.ts) are thin typed wrappers that delegate to apiFetch, each returning properly typed ApiEnvelope responses.

tour.title: Home and Search Screens
tour.description: HomeScreen.tsx is the app's landing dashboard, pulling together search, quick-scan action cards, stat cards, a trust notice with confidence badge, and recent scan history loaded via React Query. SearchScreen.tsx implements real-time product search with a text input, horizontal category chips (Drinkware, Cleaning, Packaging, Appliances), and results rendered as tappable ResultCard components. Both screens showcase the pattern used throughout: React Query for server state, theme tokens for styling, and shared UI components for consistent loading/error/empty states.

tour.title: Product Detail Flow
tour.description: The product detail flow is the core user journey. BarcodeScannerScreen manages barcode input and calls lookupBarcode, navigating to ItemDetail on success or NoMatch on failure. PhotoCaptureScreen triggers image lookups that land on CandidateResultsScreen with ranked matches. ItemDetailScreen is the richest screen in the app -- it fetches item data, displays match/confidence badges (from MatchBadge and ConfidenceBadge components), impact metric rows, materials breakdown, disposal guidance, sources list, and a save-item mutation. MetricDetailScreen drills into a single metric's methodology and data source.

tour.title: Restaurant Types and API
tour.description: The restaurant feature has its own type system. src/types/restaurant.ts defines food carbon impact types, material sustainability scan types, and the Sparks gamification types, plus a buildCarbonEquivalents utility that converts kg CO2e into relatable comparisons (miles driven, phone charges, tree absorption days). restaurantLookup.ts provides the client-side API functions: scanFoodPhoto, scanMaterial, searchMenuItem, and fetchSparksSummary. This parallel type/API structure mirrors the product lookup feature but targets the restaurant sustainability domain.

tour.title: Restaurant Hooks and Components
tour.description: Building on the restaurant types from Step 9, useRestaurantScan.ts provides three TanStack Query hooks (useFoodPhotoScan, useMaterialScan, useMenuSearch) that handle the scan-and-reward flow, automatically syncing earned Sparks to a Zustand store on success. useSparks.ts manages the gamification state with a dual-layer approach: a Zustand store for instant local badge count reads, and a TanStack Query hook for server synchronization. The restaurant components -- FoodImpactCard, MaterialImpactCard, and SparksBadge -- render the rich impact data and gamification UI.
tour.languageLesson: This dual-state pattern (Zustand for synchronous UI reads, TanStack Query for async server sync) avoids the flickering that happens when badge counts depend solely on async fetches. The Zustand store is hydrated on fetch success, giving components instant access.

tour.title: Voice Chat Feature
tour.description: The voice chat feature demonstrates a multi-service integration pipeline. useVoiceChat.ts implements a state machine that records audio via expo-av, transcribes it via whisper.ts (OpenAI Whisper API), sends the transcript with user scan history context to claude.ts (Anthropic Claude Haiku with sustainability-focused system instructions), and speaks the response aloud using expo-speech. VoiceAskScreen.tsx renders a chat bubble UI with user/assistant/error messages and text input controls. This is the most complex hook in the app, orchestrating four external services in sequence.

tour.title: Server Controllers
tour.description: Shifting to the backend, the server uses an Express controller factory pattern. lookup.ts's createLookupController instantiates all restaurant services (Vision, FoodEmission, MaterialImpact, Sparks, USDA, Climatiq) and returns a handler supporting image lookup for food and material pipelines. search.ts's createSearchController extends product search with a 'food' mode that queries the food emission table with optional USDA enrichment. Both controllers use server/types/restaurant.ts for shared request/response types and the buildCarbonEquivalents utility.

tour.title: Server Service Pipeline
tour.description: The server services implement a multi-strategy data resolution pipeline. VisionService wraps Google Cloud Vision API to identify food items and materials from photos. FoodEmissionService uses a four-stage lookup chain (exact match, alias containment, pg_trgm fuzzy matching, category fallback) against PostgreSQL. UsdaService optionally enriches results with nutritional data from USDA FoodData Central. ClimatiqService acts as a last-resort estimator using Climatiq's EXIOBASE IO tables. MaterialImpactService mirrors the food service's multi-strategy approach for disposable restaurant materials. SparksService implements the gamification reward system with transactional persistence.

tour.title: Seed Data and Dev Tooling
tour.description: The database seed files contain the reference environmental data that powers the app. food_emission_factors.ts has farm-to-fork CO2e emission factors per kg for approximately 50 food categories sourced from Agribalyse, IPCC, and Poore & Nemecek. material_impacts.ts has lifecycle impact data for disposable restaurant materials. mock-api-server.js provides a standalone HTTP server that simulates the entire Green Life REST API with hardcoded data, enabling frontend development without the real backend. Together, these files make the app self-contained for development and testing.
